title: Week 27 Check-In · By the Great Horn Spoon!
description: This week you read Chapters 7 to 9 and a real 1849 account of San Francisco. You practiced compound and complex sentences, the roots curr/curs and tract, -tion/-sion words and word families, sequence and pacing, and building the middle of an adventure. Show what you know.

questions.label: Identification
questions.text: Which sentence from Chapter 7 is a complex sentence?
options: The paddlewheels twirled, faster and faster, and the bowsprit came around on course.
When the Lady Wilma entered the blue Bay of Callao, Jack counted thirty-one sailing ships at anchor.
Jack posted another letter home to Boston.
questions.status: fixed (four options; book lines instead of made-up ones)

questions.label: Combine
questions.text: Combine the two sentences into one compound sentence. Use a comma and a joining word (and, but, so).
questions.excerpt: Water cost a dollar a bucket. Praiseworthy decided they would wait.
questions.key: Water cost a dollar a bucket, so Praiseworthy decided they would wait. (comma + and/but/so)

questions.label: Application
questions.text: Write one complex sentence about Chapter 9 that begins with Although or Because. Put a comma after the first part.
questions.key: Although/Because + dependent clause, + independent clause, about Ch. 9.

questions.label: Root
questions.text: Which word contains a root meaning pull?

questions.label: Context Clues
questions.text: Read the lines from Chapter 7. What does skedaddled mean?
questions.excerpt: “She’s loaded up with coal and fresh water,” snapped Captain Swain. “Loaded up and skedaddled!”
questions.status: new (vocabulary in context; replaces a second root-meaning item)

questions.label: Use the Word
questions.text: Use the word distraction in a sentence about Jack’s journey. Then tell how its root tract (pull) helps explain its meaning.
questions.key: A correct sentence + tract = pull, so a distraction pulls your attention away.

questions.label: Base-Word Rule
questions.text: Which word ends in -sion because its base word ends in de?
questions.status: new (the base-word rule; replaces a syllables item)

questions.label: Word Families
questions.text: Which group of words is one word family?

questions.label: Cause and Effect
questions.text: With no coal left, how does the Lady Wilma get steam up for the final sprint in Chapter 7?
options: She burns the lumber in her cargo hold.
She buys coal in the Galapagos.
The Sea Raven shares her coal.
She burns the bricks in her hold.

questions.label: Cause and Effect
questions.text: How does Quartz Jackson’s strange request turn into the answer to Jack and Praiseworthy’s money problem? Explain the chain in 2–3 sentences.
questions.key: His beard and hair hold gold dust from the diggings; Jack pans the cuttings and finds gold; Quartz gives it to them, and they start barbering to earn the fare.
questions.status: new (replaces a question about the invented passage)

questions.label: Real Account and Novel
questions.text: Bayard Taylor paid porters two dollars each and wrote that every newcomer felt “complete bewilderment.” Name one way Jack’s first day in San Francisco in Chapter 8 is like Taylor’s, with one detail from each.
questions.key: A real link (sky-high prices, crowds, confusion, people selling everything) + one detail from Taylor + one from Ch. 8.

questions.label: Poetry
questions.text: Read the line from Browning’s poem. What does the strong, repeated beat do?
questions.excerpt: I galloped, Dirck galloped, we galloped all three;
options: It makes the ride feel fast, like hoofbeats.
It tells us what the good news is.
It shows the riders are lost.

questions.label: Your Middle
questions.text: Write 4–6 sentences from the middle of your adventure. Show the steps of one tense moment in order, end that moment with one short sentence, and include one compound or complex sentence (label it).
questions.key: Steps in order + a short sentence that lands + a labeled compound or complex sentence.
questions.from: 27.1–27.4 Writer's Workshop; Read Like a Writer (pacing)
questions.status: changed (adds the pacing focus; now 1 point)

passage.title: Reading passage (Chapter 8)
passage.text: Quartz Jackson insisted that every lock be caught as it fell.
passage.cite: Sid Fleischman, By the Great Horn Spoon!, Chapter 8
